clue.text: Party united? Nonsense - riven by tense insecurities!

indicators.note: something riven is split open, so the word for nonsense is split apart to take the tense letter inside

blocks.note: a do is a party
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
BS is slang shorthand for nonsense
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A political party claiming unity is exposed as nonsense, torn apart by nervous doubts.
explanation.walkthrough: BS is the polite abbreviation of a rude word for nonsense; 'Party united?' reads as a question about politics but is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubts are feelings of uncertainty, which is what insecurities are in the plural sense.

clue.text: Arab shortly heading north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading from the bottom upwards, so the phrase runs backwards

blocks.note: 'in a mo' is informal for shortly, in a moment

explanation.surface: An Arab traveller will soon be setting off northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An Omani is a native of Oman on the Arabian peninsula, so an Arab by nationality.

clue.text: British admiral "Urgent - drifting English ships lost here"

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
admiral and urgent taken as written, plus E for English

explanation.surface: A British admiral sends an urgent signal that English ships are drifting and lost.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is ADMIRAL, URGENT and the E for English, with B standing in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bermuda Triangle is the area of the western Atlantic notorious for ships and aircraft vanishing.

clue.text: Bastard offspring stealing a gallantry medal

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bastard' looks like it describes the offspring, but it is the definition, a term of abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so is a euphemism for an unpleasant person, used in place of a ruder word such as bastard.

clue.text: Worthless Russian fighter turned to hard drug

blocks.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
crack cocaine is a hard drug

explanation.surface: A useless Russian soldier has turned to hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian fighter' suggests a soldier; in crosswords it is usually the MiG jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Gimcrack describes showy but flimsy, cheap goods, so it means worthless.

clue.text: Thoreau's gag! Fell about in fits of giggles!

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed in hysterics at one of Thoreau's jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell about' reads as one idiom for laughing hard, but 'Fell' is fodder and 'about' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gales of laughter are loud bursts of hilarity, so fits of giggles.

clue.text: Spanish trained killer boring, humdrum, a tad ordinary

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the answer is found inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of humdrum and on through 'a tad or'

explanation.surface: A trained Spanish killer is dull, humdrum and rather ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' looks like part of the list of dull adjectives, but it is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull in a Spanish corrida, a trained professional.

clue.text: Dwarf throwing? It'll impress Knut!

indicators.note: throwing scatters things about, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written; Knut is the setter

explanation.surface: The setter Knut would be impressed by a spot of dwarf-throwing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dwarf-throwing is a notorious pub stunt; here 'Dwarf' is the definition and 'throwing' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpelstiltskin is the little man of the Grimm fairy tale who spins straw into gold.

clue.text: A pair of Charlies together with Romeo start to annoy doom-monger

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet, and a charlie is also a fool, an ass
together with means and
Romeo is R in the radio alphabet
the opening letter of annoy

explanation.surface: Two idiots and a romantic lead start to irritate a pessimist.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Charlies are different: the radio-alphabet C and a 'right charlie', British slang for a fool, giving ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassandra was the Trojan prophetess doomed never to be believed, so her name means a prophet of disaster.

clue.text: Queen might have to cough up for this unfurnished vestibule, according to Spooner

definitions.text: Queen might have to cough up for this

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds of the phrase are exchanged

blocks.note: an unfurnished vestibule is a bare hall; swap the opening sounds of the two words

explanation.surface: The Queen might have to pay for a bare entrance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: A queen is a female cat, and 'cough up' means bring up as well as pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats swallow fur while grooming and bring up the matted lump, which is a hairball.

clue.text: Least demanding exam spanning the morning

indicators.note: something spanning a period stretches across it, so the exam word goes round the other

blocks.note: a test is an exam
a.m. denotes the morning

explanation.surface: The easiest exam is the one that runs through the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamest is the superlative of tame, meaning dullest or least challenging.

clue.text: £51 retired authentic Hindu put through a blender

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the next word is read backwards

desi is a South Asian word for authentic, homegrown, and for a person of Indian heritage

explanation.surface: A genuine Hindu, having retired, was mangled for fifty-one pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Read £51 as it is spoken, fifty-one quid. A quid is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To liquidise food is to blend it to a smooth liquid, so it has been put through a blender.

clue.text: Oath once occasionally seen in England?

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only alternate letters are taken

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Is this old swear word still sometimes heard in England?
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an archaic mild exclamation, a minced form of 'oh God', so an old-fashioned oath.

clue.text: Beginning to frame a kerb crawling toff out of time

indicators.note: crawling suggests moving awkwardly around, so the letters are jumbled
out of time means without the letter standing for time, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
a toff is a posh person
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A posh man is caught kerb-crawling and framed, running out of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to frame' is not a first-letter signal: in snooker each game is a frame, and the opening shot is the break-off. Kerb-crawling is soliciting from a slow car.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker the break-off is the first shot that scatters the reds and starts a frame.

clue.text: Eremitic Levi's ulcers discovered when standing up

indicators.note: discovered means with the cover taken off, so the outer letters are stripped to expose what lies inside
standing up in a down entry means reading bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters inside the two words, without the outer L and S

explanation.surface: A hermit named Levi has ulcers that are revealed when he gets up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' looks like 'found out' about the ulcers, but it means uncovered: lose the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eremitic means living like a hermit, which is what a reclusive person does.

clue.text: Make one's home chair less soft

blocks.note: to chair a meeting is to preside
p, piano, is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Settling into a new house calls for a firmer armchair.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to live there, so to make it one's home.

clue.text: Small vehicle by Autobahn, a Beetle

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a car is a vehicle
AB is a German abbreviation for Autobahn, a German motorway

explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: What might follow rag-tag old baronet detained by security?

indicators.note: someone detained is held inside, so these letters are held within the word for security

blocks.note: bail is money given as security for a defendant's return
O is the abbreviation for old
Bt is the abbreviation for baronet

explanation.surface: A scruffy old aristocrat is held on bail.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the phrase 'rag-tag and bobtail', the riff-raff.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'ragtag and bobtail' means the rabble, so bobtail follows ragtag in it.

clue.text: A Christian American lancing boils

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for American
taken as written

explanation.surface: A devout American has his boils lanced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lancing boils' reads as medical; 'boils' is the verb signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglican is a member of the Church of England or its sister churches, so one kind of Christian.

clue.text: Contradict article in spirit, perhaps

blocks.note: gin is a spirit
a is the indefinite article
say means perhaps, for example

explanation.surface: Someone disputes a newspaper article, perhaps in a defiant spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or speak against, which is to contradict.

clue.text: Ursa Minor last seen in Banana Republic

the final letter of banana

clue.text: Great cup tie broadcast run in wide vision mode?

cup tie taken as written, with R for run, the cricket abbreviation

taken as written

clue.text: Capital facial hair, Clark!
